newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which ends CRA's role as a separate entity and fulfils London-based RTZ's ambitions for a full merger of the two mining giants, RTZ-CRA announced a major management overhaul yesterday. The move will see CRA, one of Australia's largest resource companies, sack 100 staff at its Melbourne headquarters as RTZ-CRA splits into six business units. Page 1.

With a network that spans the nation, the Allens Arthur Robinson group of law firms will lose the Perth arm of its network to one of its national rivals in less than two months - effectively casting the group into the grip of mutiny. Freehill Hollingdale Page will merge in early May with the long established Perth firm of Parker and Parker. Page 5.

Amid tension between Optus Communications and U.S. West, the other major shareholder in embattled cable-TV company Optus Vision, Optus Communications is pushing to close its bid for control of Optus Vision today amid signs that Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd will sell their Vision holdings to Optus. Page 23.

In a move tipped to lead to increased competition between Qantas Airways Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd, Qantas announced the long-awaited sale of its 19.4 percent shareholding in Air NZ for NZ$425.6 million. ANZ Securities brokered the placement of Qantas' 112 million shares in regional airline at NZ$3.80 a share. Page 23.

Following two years of restructuring by AM Corporation and Perpetual Trustees (West Australia), the A$200 million Excelsior Managed Superannuation Plan will reopen next week, almost four years after computer problems caused the plan to collapse. Excelsior's 22,000 investors will have the choice of keeping their existing investments within the fund, withdrawing money or moving to an alternative fund. Page 23.

Following its move to exercise its pre-emptive right to acquire WMC Ltd's 30 percent interest in Western Australia's East Spar oil and gas interests for A$181 million, Santos Ltd announced yesterday it would raise A$270 million in a one-for-eight rights issue - the company's first capital raising in seven years. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As part of a fundamental global reorganisation, RTZ-CRA will cut 100 jobs from its Melbourne head office - a move which will split the world's biggest miner into six key commodity groups. The restructure is forecast to produce savings of up to $US60 million ($A76 million) annually. Page 19.

Qantas Airways yesterday accepted a deal for its 19.4 percent stake in Air New Zealand that will raise a pre-tax profit of $A99 million and will effectively cut all ties with its Trans-Tasman rival. The Qantas board formally accepted the offer for the 112 million B-class shares from stockbroker ANZ securities earlier this week. Page 19.

RTZ-CRA's Leon Davis yesterday confirmed an elemental change of the company's management structure, confined to history the company which fostered his success - CRA Ltd - and set in place the foundations of a business whose performance will be used to measure his place in corporate history. Page 19.

Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd effectively overrode a bid by Novus Petroleum Ltd and exercised pre-emptive rights in the battle for WMC Ltd's stake in the East Spar gas field in Western Australia. Santos said it would pay $A181 million for WMC's 30 percent stake in East Spar. Page 21.

In a bid to take 100 percent of the Argentinian $A1 billion Alumbrera copper-gold mine's copper production, partners in the project have locked in smelters around the world for when the mine begins shipments in September. MIM Holdings Ltd is expected to start production in August at a treatment rate of 80,000 tonnes of ore per day. Page 21.

In a deal worth $A1 billion, RTZ-CRA subsidiary Hamersley Iron will supply Australian United Steel Industry Ltd with iron fines for its proposed iron pellet project in Western Australia. At an iron and steel conference in Sydney yesterday, AUSI managing drector Patrick Patterson said the company had forged the 10-year supply agreement. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Stockbroking analysts reacted positively yesterday to the announcement that Qantas Airways has sold its 19.4 percent shareholding in rival Air New Zealand for about A$363 million. Qantas's 112 million Air NZ B class shares were sold to stockbroking firm ANZ Securities, which sold to a number of institutions worldwide. Page 29.

In a move which will cause Coles Myer some discomfort, the Australian Securities Commission announced yesterday it had reopened its 17-month-old investigation into the Coles-Yannon affair - one of the largest investigations ever undertaken by the Commission. Page 29.

Under a radical global restructuring plan, RTZ-CRA is to split its operations into six key commodity groups - aluminium, copper, energy, industrial minerals, iron ore and gold. The move will see CRA's corporate role drastically reduced and could lead to the resources giant becoming a branch office. Page 29.

Despite a poor result from Franklins - the discount supermarket retailer posted a A$9.7 million loss for the year to December 31 - the chain's owner, Dairy Farm International, has reaffirmed its commitment to its Australian subsidiary and has pledged A$40 million over the next four years to rebuild its reputation and gain more market share. Page 31.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, who has publicly spoken out against foreign ownership of Australia's media, has given strong indication he intends to take a high-profile role in setting new media ownership rules, confirming yesterday the Foreign Investment Review Board is also scrutinising transactions under review by the Australian Broadcasting Authority. The move adds an additional hurdle to Canadian media group CanWest retaining its 76 percent interest in the Ten Group. Page 31.

According to a survey of 360 superannuation funds by consultant Sedgwick Noble Lowndes, super fund managers are reluctant to embrace the push to allow fund members investment choice, with less than 25 percent endorsing the move. However, more than half the respondents wanted to choose their own investments five years from now. Page 31.
THE AGE

In a move which comes just 15 months after its assets merger with London-based RTZ through a dual-listed company structure, CRA looks likely to become a branch office for the London headquarters under a global restructuring plan by RTZ-CRA. About 200 jobs are to be lost in Melbourne, the United States and South Africa as the overhaul seeks to gain increased efficiencies from the combination of the global operations of the two companies. Page B1.

Payouts to long-suffering former Pyramid depositors will be cut by two to five cents in the dollar after the settlement of a $A142 million claim against the failed group of building societies. Payouts could be further reduced if Farrow Finance succeeds in a claim estimated to be worth tens of millions of dollars - adding the company to the group of creditors. Page B1.

After Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton said last month tht the airline was not seeking to sell its stake in Air New Zealand, Qantas executives denied yesterday their decision to quit the 19.4 percent stake was a change of heart. Qantas sold its 112 million B-cass shares to ANZ securities for A$373 million, severing its last tie with the rival airline. Page B1.

After more than doubling net profit for the half year to September 30 to A$674,000, Rebel Sport is on course to produce a higher profit and sales performance for the year to March 31. Rebel joint managing director Ian Dresner said yesterday the sporting goods retailer would post growth across the board for the full year. Page A3.

Under a deal that has been described as a one-off lateral solution to a marketing problem, Australia's two largest commercial radio stations, Austereo, controlled by Village Roadshow, and the Australian Radio Network, controlled by Tony O'Reilly, have formed a join venture to operate Canberra's two FM radio stations. Page B3.

The appointment of a corporate adviser on the A$450 million privatisation of the Victorian Government-owned aluminium group Aluvic, which holds a 25 percent interest in the Alcoa-managed Portland aluminium smelter joint venture, has been made, raising hopes that a sale is possible later this year. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
